summary: This Makefile defines commands to manage a Docker-based Joomla installation with a MySQL database. It provides shortcuts for common operations like starting/stopping containers, viewing logs, resetting data, and importing backups—while automatically passing the current user and group IDs to Docker to avoid permission issues. The file also loads environment variables from a .env file and displays formatted configuration information to the user.

explanations.1: This includes the .env file if it exists, loading environment variables (like WEB_PORT, DB_USER, etc.) that are referenced throughout the Makefile.
explanations.4: The $$(id -u) and $$(id -g) capture the current user and group IDs before running docker compose, ensuring containers run with matching permissions to avoid file ownership problems.
explanations.6: This makes 'down' depend on 'stop' first, so running 'make down' will stop containers before removing them.
explanations.13: The '-' prefix suppresses errors if these directories don't exist, preventing the reset task from failing.
explanations.16: The '@' suppresses echoing the command itself, so only the output appears; 'clear' wipes the terminal.
explanations.17: The \033 codes are ANSI escape sequences that add colored formatting to terminal output; ${WEB_PORT} substitutes the variable value.
explanations.39: Creates the data directories if they don't exist; '-@' suppresses both command output and errors.
explanations.40: The --detach flag runs containers in the background, and --build rebuilds images from the Dockerfile.
explanations.43: The 'import' task depends on 'reset', so it first clears old data before restoring from backup.
explanations.53: Copies the Akeeba Kickstart initialization file into the joomla_data volume so Docker can access it.
explanations.55: Copies the Kickstart restoration script into the joomla_data directory.
explanations.61: Copies the backup archive (jpa file) into the joomla_data volume for the Kickstart script to restore.
explanations.65: Starts containers without rebuilding images, allowing the Kickstart script to run and restore the backup.
